name: Post-Laminectomy Instability
definition: Mechanical instability or progressive deformity occurring after decompressive laminectomy due to loss of posterior structural support.

investigations.principle: Standing and dynamic radiographs assess instability; MRI/CT evaluate neural compression and bony anatomy.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, cartilage, occult injury, postoperative or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Progressive instability or deformity may require fusion/reconstruction.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Postoperative Sandhi-asthirata phenotype may be documented descriptively.

patientEducation.summary: Mechanical instability or progressive deformity occurring after decompressive laminectomy due to loss of posterior structural support.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, major trauma, respiratory distress, progressive neurological deficit, open injury, severe deformity, infection or other listed red flags.
